newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corn growers oppose ethanol tax repeal.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corn growers oppose ethanol tax repeal.

text.p: U.S. corn growers will let lawmakers know they oppose repeal of the ethanol tax incentive when they gather in Washington later this month, said Wallie Hardie, head of the National Corn Growers Association (NCGA).
"Ethanol is going to be critical to us as we go to the Hill in the middle of March," Hardie told reporters after the grower group voted on policies for the year at its annual convention.

Hardie said corn growers also want to hear from Washington on crop revenue coverage and what new insurance products might come up in 1998. Some 100 NCGA members will meet in the nation's capital in March for a spring board meeting.
Hardie said corn growers are pleased with the new Freedom to Farm law and want to stay course and "give it a chance to work."
At the three-day meeting, held jointly with the American Soybean Association, corn growers also reaffirmed support for maintaining 36.4 million acres enrolled in the Conservation Reserve Program.
"We feel those acres are out there, fragile lands that really should be protected...," Hardie said.
On biotech, Hardie said the grower group voted to continue to support biotech but wanted to be sure antitrust laws were being adhered to by the companies involved in the technology.
